findings.description:
The statement is `∃ (A B : Finset ℂ), A.card = B.card ∧ prodMultiset A 3 = prodMultiset B 3 ∧ A ≠ B`. Nothing forces |A| > 3. If |A| = |B| ≤ 2, `Finset.powersetCard 3` is empty, so both product multisets are `0` and any two distinct sets of equal size are witnesses. If |A| = |B| = 3, each multiset is just the singleton product (e.g. {1,2,3} vs {1,-1,-6}). So the theorem does not capture Steinerberger's counterexample (|A| = 4 > k = 3), which is what its docstring claims. It is provable in a few lines, as I checked in a scratch file:
```lean
example : type_of% Erdos494.erdos_494.variants.product := by
  refine ⟨{0}, {1}, by simp, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp only [Erdos494.prodMultiset]
    rw [Finset.powersetCard_eq_empty.mpr (by simp), Finset.powersetCard_eq_empty.mpr (by simp)]
  · simp
```
This compiles against the checked-out repo. The same degenerate-witness pattern was treated as a misformalization in past fixes (e.g. PR #4057 for Erdős 274, PR #5030 for VCDimConvex).
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/494 (Wayback snapshot 2026-09-15): "(In [Er61] Erdős states this problem incorrectly, replacing sums with products. This product formulation is easily seen to be false, as observed by Steinerberger: consider the case k=3 and subsets of the 6th roots of unity corresponding to {0,1,2,4} and {0,2,3,4} (as subsets of Z/6Z).)" The same page, on the sum version: "Kruyt notes that this is trivially false if |A|=k ... Presumably some condition like '|A| sufficiently large' is intended." So the source's counterexample uses |A| = 4 > k, and cases with |A| ≤ k are regarded as trivial and unintended.
findings.suggested_fix: Force a nondegenerate size. Either `∃ (A B : Finset ℂ), A.card = 4 ∧ B.card = 4 ∧ prodMultiset A 3 = prodMultiset B 3 ∧ A ≠ B` (or `3 < A.card ∧ A.card = B.card ∧ …`), or state Steinerberger's sets explicitly: with ζ := Complex.exp (2 * π * Complex.I / 6), take A = {1, ζ, ζ^2, ζ^4}, B = {1, ζ^2, ζ^3, ζ^4} and assert `prodMultiset A 3 = prodMultiset B 3 ∧ A ≠ B`.

reformulations.difference: Wikipedia characterises Giuga numbers by ∑_{p|n} 1/p − ∏_{p|n} 1/p ∈ ℕ. The Lean uses ∑_{p|n} 1/p − 1/n = m with m : ℕ, and the weak-Giuga predicate is n ∣ 1 + ∑_{i=1}^{n-1} i^φ(n).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For composite n, both sides force n squarefree. If p² | n, then modulo p the power sum is (#i ≤ n−1 with p ∤ i) = n − n/p ≡ 0, so n ∤ 1 + sum. Also, writing n = rad(n)·s with s > 1 and q | s, the quantity ∑1/p − 1/n = (s∑ rad/p − 1)/n has numerator ≡ −1 (mod q), so it is not an integer. For squarefree n, CRT gives: n | 1 + sum ⇔ ∀p|n, p | n/p − 1 ⇔ n | ∑ n/p − 1 ⇔ ∑1/p − 1/n ∈ ℤ, and this is positive, hence in ℕ. The Lean's 1/n in fact avoids the prime-power case where Wikipedia's ∑1/p − ∏1/p equals 0.

reformulations.difference: The source quantifies over arbitrary functions f(x) → ∞. The Lean takes f : ℕ → ℕ with f → ∞, and N / f N uses Lean real division (x/0 = 0).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given a real g → ∞, apply the Lean statement to f = ⌊g⌋₊. For large N, 0 < f(N) ≤ g(N), so |A∩[1,N]| > N/f(N) ≥ N/g(N). The converse is a special case. The finitely many N with f N = 0 do not affect 'infinitely many N'.

reformulations.difference: Heath-Brown: at least one of 2, 3, 5 is a primitive root for infinitely many primes. Lean: the set of primes p for which one of 2, 3, 5 is a primitive root is infinite.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: By pigeonhole, if infinitely many primes have one of three bases as a primitive root, one fixed base works for infinitely many of them. The converse is immediate.

reformulations.difference: The source ranges over non-constant monic polynomials with all roots real in [−1,1]. The Lean supremum also admits f = 1, and it carries an unused parameter (n : ℕ).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For f = 1 the set {x : |f x| < 1} is empty and has volume 0. Adding it to a supremum of nonnegative values in ℝ≥0∞ changes nothing, so the supremum is still 2√2.

review.notes:
The file under review only lists 100 declaration names plus a compile-time category check. It compiles, and the `verifyCategoryCounts` check passes (test 34 / research solved 50 / API 9 / textbook 7). So I reviewed each of the 100 referenced declarations against its source. 48 of them are fully proved in the repo; for the sorry'd tests I checked the values independently: the Petersen graph's 15 edges and residue 3 via native_decide in a scratch file, the tetrahedral SIC overlaps by hand, EHS numbers 8, 9, 13, …, 17 against A064164, and W(3,15) = 218 against the AKS table.

Observations that are not findings:
(1) Erdős 1067: erdosproblems.com/1067 says "Thomassen [Th17] constructed a counterexample to the version which asks for infinite edge-connectivity". Thomassen's own abstract (Combinatorica 37 (2017), DTU Orbit) says he proved that every graph of uncountable chromatic number has a subgraph with uncountable chromatic number and infinite edge-connectivity. So the file's `answer(True)` for `erdos_1067.variants.infinite_edge_connectivity` agrees with the primary source; the website remark appears to be wrong.
(2) Erdős 26: the `variants.rusza` docstring ("If we allow ∑1/a < ∞ then Ruzsa has found a counter-example") reflects an older page. The page now attributes the trivial ∑1/a < ∞ counterexample to Davenport–Erdős, and Ruzsa's construction to the unrestricted question. The Lean statement is still true.
(3) Erdős 198 `variants.concrete` uses {n!+n}, while the page gives AlphaProof's example as {(n+1)!+n}. Both are Sidon and meet every infinite AP, so the statement is fine.
(4) Green 29 `variant` drops S ⊆ A. Green's list phrases the known result with S ⊂ A, but the cited Breuillard–Green–Tao survey states the Croot–Sisask/Sanders theorem without that requirement, and the Lean matches it.
(5) Erdős 442 `variants.tao` follows Tao's Theorem 1.1 with C₀ = 1 exactly: an equality asymptotic and a sum over all pairs. That is stronger than the page's '≫' paraphrase.
(6) Erdős 349 `exists_t_for_k_disjoint_segments` formalises "at least k disjoint line segments" as "at least k connected components". Graham's claim implies it, so it is harmless.
(7) The OEIS A228828 test `a_2 : a 2 = 7` uses 0-indexed `Nat.nth`; OEIS has offset 1, so 7 is OEIS a(3). This is naming only.
(8) Outside this subset: Wikipedia now reports explicit Hadamard matrices of order 668 (Aug 2026). That bears on `Hadamard.HadamardConjecture.variants.«167»` (tagged research open), not on the listed `first_cases`.
(9) Answer polarities of the fixed answers in the subset are all correct: Erdős 457 (True), WOWII 33 (False), Erdős 965 generalization (False; Soukup–Weiss give a single ZFC colouring for all N ≥ 2), Green 14 quadratic (False), Erdős 1067 edge-connectivity (True).

demonstrated.claim: The statement as formalized (`∃ A B : Finset ℂ, A.card = B.card ∧ prodMultiset A 3 = prodMultiset B 3 ∧ A ≠ B`, taken verbatim via `type_of%`) is proved with the degenerate witnesses A = {0}, B = {1}: a singleton has no 3-element subsets, so both product multisets are empty. So it does not capture Steinerberger's 4-element counterexample that the docstring describes.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.Subsets.FC100SolvedSet1

/-!
Trivial proof of a misformalized "research solved" statement.
-/

open Erdos494

/-- `Erdos494.erdos_494.variants.product` is meant to record Steinerberger's counterexample to
the product version of Erdős 494 (two distinct 4-element sets with equal multisets of 3-fold
products). As stated it is provable with the degenerate witnesses `A = {0}`, `B = {1}`:
a 1-element set has no 3-element subsets, so both product multisets are empty. -/
example : type_of% @Erdos494.erdos_494.variants.product := by
  refine ⟨{0}, {1}, by simp, ?_, by simp⟩
  -- both multisets of 3-fold products are empty, since `powersetCard 3` of a singleton is `∅`
  simp only [prodMultiset]
  rw [Finset.powersetCard_eq_empty.mpr (by simp), Finset.powersetCard_eq_empty.mpr (by simp)]

/-- The degenerate witnesses really have no 3-fold products at all. -/
example : prodMultiset ({0} : Finset ℂ) 3 = 0 ∧ prodMultiset ({1} : Finset ℂ) 3 = 0 := by
  constructor <;>
  · simp only [prodMultiset]
    rw [Finset.powersetCard_eq_empty.mpr (by simp)]
    rfl

not_fixed.reason: Needs changes outside the only editable file: the theorem is defined in FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/494.lean, and FC100SolvedSet1.lean only lists it by name via `decl_name%`. Proposed replacement in 494.lean (keep the name and `@[category research solved, AMS 5]`): `theorem erdos_494.variants.product : ∃ (A B : Finset ℂ), 3 < A.card ∧ A.card = B.card ∧ prodMultiset A 3 = prodMultiset B 3 ∧ A ≠ B`. The docstring should say that sets of size ≤ 3 are excluded because their 3-fold product multiset is empty or a single product, and that Steinerberger's sets have size 4. I checked in /workspace/review/fix494.lean, against the repo's own `Erdos494.prodMultiset`, that this statement elaborates, excludes the old degenerate witness A = {0}, B = {1}, and is provable with a genuine witness: A = {1,2,3,4} and B = ω·A for a primitive cube root of unity ω. That proof uses only the standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The existing `formal_proof` link was written for the old, degenerate statement and I did not open it (it is a fork of the repository on GitHub), so maintainers should check it still applies or remove it.
